hotkeys.query: OpenWhispr dictation hotkeys shortcuts hold tap activation mode
hotkeys.text: Open Settings → App → Hotkeys. Click the shortcut field and press the combination you want; it saves when registration succeeds, with no separate Save or Apply button. Activation Mode is directly below Dictation Hotkey: Tap means press once to start and again to stop; Hold means hold while speaking and release to stop. Hold applies to dictation only and availability depends on your platform and shortcut. Voice Assistant, Translation and Meeting Mode have separate shortcuts. Activation mode controls when recording starts and stops; it does not decide where audio is processed or guarantee local-only processing.

microphone.query: OpenWhispr choose microphone permissions no audio
microphone.text: Open Settings → App → Preferences → Input Device. Choose a microphone or System Default, which follows the operating system input choice. Review microphone permission under Settings → System → Privacy & Data. A saved choice or granted permission does not prove recording works. Waiting for microphone is not a diagnosis of permission denial: the device may be unavailable, still opening or recovering. Check the selected device and input level while speaking; inspect permissions if access is denied.

models.query: OpenWhispr local models speech to text language models configuration
models.text: Speech-to-text turns audio into words; language models handle cleanup, Voice Assistant and Chat answers. For offline dictation choose and download a local speech model under Settings → AI Models → Speech-to-Text → Dictation → Local. Dictation, Note Recording and Audio Upload each have their own speech-to-text selection. For local Chat separately choose and download a supported local language model under Settings → AI Models → Language Models → Chat → Local. Use the in-app catalog for currently available models. Cleanup and Voice Assistant have independent language-model selections too. Download required models before going offline. A local speech model alone does not make Chat local. Hold is an activation mode, not a processing/privacy control. Cloud backup and connected tools are separate network features; these selections do not guarantee the whole app is offline.

meetings.query: OpenWhispr record meeting system audio permission speaker labels
meetings.text: Meeting recordings use microphone audio for your voice and system audio for other participants. Check permissions under Settings → System → Privacy & Data. Choose the recording engine under Settings → AI Models → Speech-to-Text → Note Recording. Connecting a calendar is optional for starting a recording; it does not grant audio permissions. Waiting for microphone means the input is reconnecting or unavailable, not necessarily that permission was denied. Check your selected input device and its connection, then review microphone permission. A saved permission status is not a recording test.

calendar.query: OpenWhispr connect calendar Google Microsoft Apple meetings
calendar.text: Open Integrations → Calendars to review calendar connections. Calendar access and meeting audio capture are separate: connecting a calendar does not grant microphone or system audio permission.

language.query: OpenWhispr interface language transcription language translation
language.text: Interface language and Transcription language are separate settings under Settings → App → Preferences. Transcription language applies across recording activities. Translation is a separate feature with its own shortcut and target language.

backup.query: OpenWhispr cloud backup sync notes devices local storage
backup.text: Cloud backup controls syncing notes across devices. It is separate from the model used for transcription or assistant answers. Your organisation may restrict backup or processing choices.

assistant.query: OpenWhispr chat agent tools model availability voice assistant
assistant.text: Choose the Chat language model under Settings → AI Models → Language Models → Chat, separately from speech-to-text, cleanup and Voice Assistant. Tool availability depends on the model, connections and organisation policy. Small or unrecognised local models may run without tools. Product help in Chat can show reviewed guidance and read-only current settings even when the selected model cannot answer. If a provider request fails, retry or review the selected Chat provider and model; help cannot verify credentials or service availability from saved settings.
